- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- When sentiment flips sharply (e.g., from bullish to bearish), model lags; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% in first 2–3 days post-sentiment shift.
- If model shows strong upward trend after a spike, true price often corrects; apply mean reversion: subtract 1–3% from forecast if price > 20% above 10-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates near end of forecast; reduce final 5–7 days by 1–2% to align with observed tapering.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.33/1.00), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before final output.
